cards.front: Recall a key point about Stakeholders
cards.back: Stakeholders: any person or group with an interest in a business. Internal: owners, employees, managers. External: customers, suppliers, local community, government, pressure groups.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stakeholders
cards.back: Stakeholder objectives often conflict: owners want maximum profit (low wages, high prices); employees want higher wages and better conditions; customers want low prices and high quality; local community wants jobs but less pollution; government wants tax revenue and compliance.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stakeholders
cards.back: Managing stakeholder conflict: compromise, negotiation, prioritisation. Businesses cannot satisfy all stakeholders equally - they must balance competing interests based on power and importance.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stakeholders
cards.back: Stakeholder influence varies: owners/shareholders have high influence (can appoint directors); employees can take industrial action; customers can take their business elsewhere; pressure groups can damage reputation through social media campaigns.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stakeholders
cards.back: Stakeholder mapping: power (ability to influence) vs interest (how much they care). High power + high interest = key players who must be managed closely.

cards.front: What should you know about business exam tips?
cards.back: For stakeholder questions: 1) Identify all relevant stakeholders, 2) State each one's objective, 3) Identify the conflict, 4) Suggest how the business could manage it, 5) Evaluate which stakeholder has the most influence and why.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: All stakeholders are equally important and businesses must treat them all the same. Correct: Stakeholders have different levels of power and interest. Shareholders in a plc have significant influence through voting rights; a local community group may have strong feelings but limited direct power (though social media can amplify their voice). AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of Stakeholders with precise business/economic terminology. Define key terms and state accurate factual information.

Stakeholders is a key topic in GCSE Business Studies that affects how businesses operate in the UK economy. Understanding this concept requires knowledge of both theoretical principles and real-world application. The AQA specification requires you to explain, analyse and evaluate business concepts using appropriate terminology, and apply them to real business scenarios using UK examples.

cards.front: Applying Stakeholders to UK Business Examples
cards.back: For stakeholders, applying theory to practice means using real UK business examples to illustrate your understanding. Small businesses face different challenges from large corporations when dealing with stakeholders. Consider how factors like business size, ownership structure, industry sector and market position affect the impact of stakeholders on a business.

GCSE Business exam questions about stakeholders range from 1-mark definition questions to 12-mark evaluation questions. For definition questions (1-2 marks), give a precise business definition. For explanation questions (3-4 marks), define and explain with a brief example. For analysis questions (6-9 marks), develop a chain of reasoning showing cause and effect.
